inputs.original_text: TAOISEACH Micheál Martin, speaking in Limerick this past week, said that housing tenancies have increased despite concern at a rise in eviction notices and homelessness in the wake of new rules, introduced by Government on March 1, forcing landlords to provide six-year leases for tenants. The numbers of people in emergency accommodation nationally increased again [...] The post Taoiseach says housing tenancies have increased despite rise in eviction notices and homelessness appeared first on Limerick Post .
inputs.modified_text: The Taoiseach is out in Limerick claiming housing tenancies have risen even after his government's March 1 rules forced landlords into six-year leases, while brushing off the spike in eviction notices and homelessness. Yet the numbers of people in emergency accommodation have climbed again nationally. This is the predictable result of heavy-handed government interference in private rental agreements, undermining property rights and family stability instead of letting personal responsibility and market signals maintain order.
